page: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is a memory-optimized cloud compute instance within the VX1 family, equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The system provides 64 GB of system memory, yielding a generous 8 GB of RAM per vCPU (1:8 core-to-memory ratio). It features 32 MB of shared L3 cache, 1 MB L2 cache, and supports advanced vector extensions including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, alongside hardware cryptographic instruction sets such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Storage configuration is minimal, providing only a 1 GB local NVMe SSD boot disk and no hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating network storage attachments for persistent or large-scale data storage. Benchmark metrics demonstrate exceptional single-thread capabilities, scoring in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng operations, single-thread gzip compression at 39.67 GB/sec, and single-thread bzip3 decompression at 17.67 GB/sec. Geekbench single-core performance places in the top 25%, while multi-core metrics, PassMark evaluations, and uncached large-block memory bandwidth (72.42 GB/sec read, 41.4 GB/sec write) place squarely in the middle 50% tier.

The instance delivers strong qualitative value for in-memory and memory-dense workloads due to its dedicated core allocation and high memory ratio. However, multi-core throughput scaling is moderate, and prompt processing for larger LLM architectures (such as 7B models) exhibits lower relative efficiency. vx1-m-8c-64gb is particularly suited for high-density caching, in-memory databases like Redis, medium-scale ETL, memory-intensive compilation pipelines, and single-thread-sensitive web microservices.
description: Vultr vx1-m-8c-64gb is a memory-optimized cloud instance providing 8 dedicated vCPUs from an AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 64 GB of RAM and a minimal 1 GB local NVMe boot disk. Designed for applications requiring high memory density relative to core count, the instance features an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and supports AVX-512 vector acceleration. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core execution speed and compression performance alongside solid mid-range multi-core processing and memory bandwidth. With zero GPU accelerators and negligible local disk capacity, persistent workloads will depend on secondary storage volumes. The instance represents an efficient infrastructure choice for memory-intensive applications, caching servers like Redis, transactional databases, and batch data processing where dedicated CPU stability and large memory capacity are primary requirements.
